citations.quote:
Assume the Axiom of Choice ([[def-axiom-of-choice]]). Fix an integer $n\ge1$ and an open phase-coordinate domain $O_{\rm phys}\subseteq\mathbb R^{2n}$ with physical canonical coordinates $q_i$ in metres and $p_i$ in $\mathrm{kg\,m\,s^{-1}}$. The canonical symplectic form on this chart is $\omega_{\rm phys}=\sum_{i=1}^n dq_i\wedge dp_i$. Let $\hat q_i=q_i/(1\,\mathrm m)$ and $\hat p_i=p_i/(1\,\mathrm{kg\,m\,s^{-1}})$, and let $O\subseteq\mathbb R^{2n}$ be the open image of the chart in these dimensionless coordinates. The corresponding dimensionless canonical form is $\hat\omega=\sum_{i=1}^n d\hat q_i\wedge d\hat p_i$, so $\omega_{\rm phys}=(1\,\mathrm{J\,s})\hat\omega$.

Let $\hat H:O\to\mathbb R$ be a numerical energy function with continuous partial derivatives through order two, and let $H_{\rm phys}:O_{\rm phys}\to\mathbb R\,\mathrm J$ be $H_{\rm phys}(q,p)=(1\,\mathrm J)\hat H(\hat q,\hat p)$. Where defined, its physical Hamiltonian vector field $X_{H_{\rm phys}}$ is determined by $\iota_{X_{H_{\rm phys}}}\omega_{\rm phys}=dH_{\rm phys}$. For each elapsed time $t$ in its domain, the physical flow map is a function $\phi_t:D_t\to O_{\rm phys}$, where $D_t\subseteq O_{\rm phys}$ is the set of initial data whose trajectories exist through time $t$, and it satisfies $d\phi_t/dt=X_{H_{\rm phys}}\circ\phi_t$. Equivalently, in the dimensionless chart, the flow map $\hat\phi_{\hat t}:\hat D_{\hat t}\to O$ is generated by $X_{\hat H}$ satisfying $\iota_{X_{\hat H}}\hat\omega=d\hat H$, at dimensionless time $\hat t=t/(1\,\mathrm s)$; here $\hat D_{\hat t}$ is the set of initial coordinates whose trajectories exist through $\hat t$. These definitions specify the flow maps when they exist but impose no global-existence or completeness hypothesis on the shell preparation.

A specified open interval $J_E\subseteq\mathbb R$ is a regular compact-shell band when $\hat H^{-1}(K)$ is compact in $O$ for every compact $K\subset J_E$ and $\nabla\hat H$ is nonzero at every point of $\hat H^{-1}(J_E)$.

For $\hat E\in J_E$, the energy shell is $\Sigma_{\hat E}:=\{x\in O:\hat H(x)=\hat E\}$. The graph-chart definition of the weighted shell integral is [[def-tdmath-regular-energy-shell]]: in a local graph chart $x_i=h(z,\hat E)$, its coarea measure is $d\mu_{\hat E}=dA_{\hat E}/|\nabla\hat H|$, with graph-area factor and gradient in the dimensionless Euclidean coordinates. Set $D(\hat E):=\int_{\Sigma_{\hat E}}d\mu_{\hat E}$ and admit the preparation only when $\Sigma_{\hat E}\ne\varnothing$ and $0<D(\hat E)<\infty$. Its normalized shell law is $\nu_{\hat E}(A):=D(\hat E)^{-1}\mu_{\hat E}(A\cap\Sigma_{\hat E})$. The current draft theorem [[thm-tdmath-regular-energy-shell-measure]] proves the coarea identity, chart independence and positive finite shell mass under its stated $C^2$, compact-regular-band hypotheses; its statement and proof are present, while its acceptance remains unresolved. Multiplying the unnormalized shell measure by a fixed positive phase-volume normalization does not change $\nu_{\hat E}$.

For the regular-shell branch below, assume AC as required by
[[def-td-regular-hamiltonian-shell-preparation]] and its coarea-measure
supplier. No choice assumption is needed for the separate finite-window branch.

For a finite microstate model and a declared energy value $E_0$ in joules and resolution $\delta\ge0$ in joules, define the admitted window
$$\Omega_{E_0,\delta}:=\{x\in\Omega:|E(x)-E_0|\le\delta\}.$$
When this set is nonempty, adopt the uniform preparation $P(x)=|\Omega_{E_0,\delta}|^{-1}$ on it and zero outside. Its dimensionless Boltzmann entropy is $\log|\Omega_{E_0,\delta}|$, and its physical entropy convention is $k_{\mathrm B}\log|\Omega_{E_0,\delta}|$ in $\mathrm{J\,K^{-1}}$. A zero-width window is allowed only when it contains at least one microstate.

For a continuous classical model, when the regular-band, nonempty-shell, and normalization hypotheses in [[def-td-regular-hamiltonian-shell-preparation]] hold, the microcanonical preparation is the normalized shell measure $\nu_{\hat E}$ defined there. The shell preparation does not require a globally defined flow. These finite-window and regular-shell rules are adopted model preparations. They do not assert Hamiltonian ergodicity, equality with long-time averages, canonical sampling, or equilibration.

Assume the Axiom of Choice. Let $(M,\omega)$ be a smooth $2n$-dimensional symplectic manifold and $H\in C^\infty(M,\mathbb R)$, with Hamiltonian field defined by $\iota_{X_H}\omega=dH$. Wherever its local flow $\phi_t$ is defined, it preserves the symplectic form and the volume measure $m$ determined by $\omega^n/n!$. No completeness is asserted. Let $R$ be a measurable region on which a nonzero-time map $T=\phi_\tau$ is defined and is forward invariant, $T(R)\subseteq R$. The restriction $T:R\to R$ preserves $m|_R$ if $T(R)=R$, or more generally if $m(R\setminus T(R))=0$. This latter condition holds automatically when $m(R)<\infty$. Thus for every finite-measure forward-invariant $R$ and every measurable $E\subseteq R$, almost every point of $E$ returns to $E$ infinitely often under forward iteration. Mere forward invariance of an infinite-volume region does not imply relative measure preservation.

If $m(R)=1$ and $T$ is ergodic, then for every $f\in L^1(R,m)$ the averages $N^{-1}\sum_{j=0}^{N-1}f(T^jx)$ converge almost everywhere and in $L^1$ to $\int_Rf\,dm$. Without ergodicity, the limit is the invariant conditional expectation supplied by Birkhoff's theorem, not necessarily the space mean. Finally, fix any real scalar $k_B$. If each stated time map $\phi_t$ is a diffeomorphism of a finite invariant region $R$, a density $p_0\ge0$ with $\int_Rp_0\,dm=1$ and $\int_R|p_0\log p_0|\,dm<\infty$ transports by $p_t=p_0\circ\phi_{-t}$ with conserved fine-grained entropy $-k_B\int_Rp_t\log p_t\,dm$, using $0\log0=0$. Volume preservation alone does not imply ergodicity or a time-average/ensemble identity.

Assume AC. Let $n\ge1$, let $O\subset\mathbb R^{2n}$ be open with its canonical symplectic form, let $H\in C^2(O,\mathbb R)$, and let $J\subset\mathbb R$ be open. Suppose $\nabla H\ne0$ on $H^{-1}(J)$ and $H^{-1}(K)$ is compact in $O$ for every compact $K\subset J$. Define $\mu_E$ by [[def-tdmath-regular-energy-shell]]. Then for every nonnegative Borel $f$ compactly supported in $H^{-1}(J)$,
$$\int_Of(x)\,dx=\int_J\mu_E(f)\,dE.$$
For every $E\in J$ with nonempty shell $\Sigma_E=H^{-1}(\{E\})$, $0<\mu_E(1)<\infty$, and $\widehat\mu_E=\mu_E/\mu_E(1)$ is a probability measure. Let $\phi_t$ be a Hamiltonian flow map defined as a diffeomorphism on a full compact energy band containing $\Sigma_E$ and preserving that band. Then $\widehat\mu_E$ is invariant under $\phi_t$ for every such regular $E$. Critical levels and noncompact bands are outside this statement.

derivations.claim: By [F1] and [A2], the canonical Hamiltonian data, smoothness, and full-band invertible flow match the hypotheses of [L1]–[L2]. In dimensionless time, energy is conserved along each flow line because $\frac{d}{d\hat t}\hat H(\hat\phi_{\hat t}(x))=d\hat H(X_{\hat H})=\hat\omega(X_{\hat H},X_{\hat H})=0$; the global-flow condition is an assumption, not a consequence of local equations.

The draft suppliers [L1] and [L2] give volume preservation and shell-measure invariance for the matched model in step 1.1. Normalization by the positive finite shell mass preserves invariance, and [F2] assigns that normalized measure as the preparation. Hence $\nu_{\hat E}(\phi_t^{-1}(A))=\nu_{\hat E}(A)$. This deduction remains conditional while both suppliers lack current Step 1 readiness.

case_scope.source_excerpt:
Let a physical Hamiltonian model satisfy [[def-td-regular-hamiltonian-shell-preparation]] on a nonempty compact regular energy band, and adopt its normalized shell law by [[post-td-microcanonical-sampling]]. In addition to the definition's $C^2$ regularity, assume its numerical Hamiltonian $\hat H$ is $C^\infty$. Let $\phi_t$ be the physical Hamiltonian flow defined there, with $t$ measured in seconds, and assume it is an invertible smooth map of the whole band for every real time. Then, conditional on the current batch-12 draft mathematical interfaces [[thm-tdmath-hamiltonian-measure-and-recurrence]] and [[thm-tdmath-regular-energy-shell-measure]], every shell probability $
u_{\hat E}$ is invariant:
$$
u_{\hat E}(\phi_t^{-1}(A))=
u_{\hat E}(A)$$
for every Borel set $A\subseteq\Sigma_{\hat E}$ and every $t\in\mathbb R$. This result asserts no ergodicity, time-average equality, or thermalization.

citations.quote: Fix integers $d\ge1$, $L\ge1$, a finite alphabet $\mathcal A$ of cardinality $q\ge1$, and a finite, possibly empty, list of interaction shapes $S_a\subset\mathbb Z^d$, each nonempty and contained in $[-R,R]^d$ for some integer $R\ge0$. $\|\Phi_a\|_\infty$ is finite because its domain is finite. For each shape let $\Phi_a:\mathcal A^{S_a}\to\mathbb R$ be a bounded interaction function. Set $J_0:=\sum_a\|\Phi_a\|_\infty$. On $\Lambda_L:=\{1,\ldots,L\}^d$, define the free-boundary energy $H_L(s):=\sum_a\sum_{x:x+S_a\subseteq\Lambda_L}\Phi_a((s_{x+u})_{u\in S_a})$, for configurations $s\in\mathcal A^{\Lambda_L}$. For $\beta>0$, define the finite partition sum $Z_L(\beta):=\sum_{s\in\mathcal A^{\Lambda_L}}e^{-\beta H_L(s)}$ and normalized log-partition density $p_L(\beta):=L^{-d}\log Z_L(\beta)$.

For every fixed $\beta>0$, the sequence $p_L(\beta)$ of [[def-tdmath-bounded-finite-range-lattice]] has a finite limit as $L\to\infty$. If another finite-volume energy $\widetilde H_L$ on the same configurations satisfies $\sup_s|\widetilde H_L(s)-H_L(s)|\le C_bL^{d-1}$ for a constant $C_b$ independent of $L$, define $\widetilde Z_L(\beta):=\sum_{s\in\mathcal A^{\Lambda_L}}e^{-\beta\widetilde H_L(s)}$ and $\widetilde p_L(\beta):=L^{-d}\log\widetilde Z_L(\beta)$. Then $\widetilde p_L$ has the same limit. The result covers finite-alphabet, bounded, translation-invariant finite-range interactions on cubic boxes; it asserts no continuum-particle or long-range limit.

This framework uses the modern International System of Units (SI). A scalar quantity has a real numerical value with the stated unit; a vector quantity has a value in the stated real coordinate space with the stated component unit. The numerical coordinates used elsewhere on this page are divided by their displayed SI units before they are placed in a Euclidean coordinate space.

The model's energy coordinate $U$ and its process-transfer values $Q$ and $W_{\mathrm{on}}$ are scalar energies measured in joules (J). Volume $V$ is a scalar measured in cubic metres (m³); amount of substance $n_j$ for species $j$ is a scalar measured in moles (mol); and a particle count $N_j$, when separately used in a microscopic model, is dimensionless. Time $t$ is measured in seconds (s), mass $M$ in kilograms (kg), and a translational velocity $\mathbf v_{\mathrm{cm}}$ is a vector in $\mathbb R^3$ with components measured in metres per second (m/s). The physical meanings of $U,Q,W_{\mathrm{on}}$ are fixed by the state and process definitions, not by their units alone.

The relevant exact SI relations are

$$1\,\mathrm J=1\,\mathrm{kg\,m^2\,s^{-2}},\qquad 1\,\mathrm N=1\,\mathrm{kg\,m\,s^{-2}},\qquad 1\,\mathrm{Pa}=1\,\mathrm{J\,m^{-3}}.$$

The kelvin (K) is the SI unit of thermodynamic temperature. The Boltzmann constant has the exact defining value $k_{\mathrm B}=1.380649\times10^{-23}\,\mathrm{J\,K^{-1}}$. The mole is the SI unit of amount of substance; the Avogadro constant has the exact defining value $N_{\mathrm A}=6.02214076\times10^{23}\,\mathrm{mol^{-1}}$. When a model uses particle counts, $n_j=N_j/N_{\mathrm A}$. The molar gas constant is derived as $R=N_{\mathrm A}k_{\mathrm B}=8.31446261815324\,\mathrm{J\,mol^{-1}\,K^{-1}}$. This framework does not set $k_{\mathrm B}=1$. These SI definitions do not themselves introduce a thermodynamic temperature state function or entropy function.

Within the macroscopic framework, $(U,V,n_j)$ are adopted state coordinates. A quantity's status as primitive in this model is separate from whether its SI unit is a base or derived unit.

Assign a positive temperature $T$ in kelvins and the exact framework constant $k_{\mathrm B}$ in $\mathrm{J\,K^{-1}}$ from [[def-td-si-quantities]], and put $\beta=(k_{\mathrm B}T)^{-1}$ in $\mathrm{J^{-1}}$. For a finite microstate model $(\Omega,\epsilon)$, adopt the canonical preparation
$$P_\beta(x)=\frac{e^{-\beta E(x)}}{Z(\beta)},\qquad Z(\beta)=\sum_{x\in\Omega}e^{-\beta E(x)}.$$
Here $Z$ is dimensionless, positive, and finite because $\Omega$ is finite and nonempty.

citations.quote: A measure space is a triple $(X,\Sigma,\mu)$ where $\Sigma$ contains $\varnothing,X$ and is closed under complements and countable unions (a $\sigma$-algebra) of subsets of $X$ and $\mu:\Sigma\to[0,\infty]$ is countably additive with $\mu(\varnothing)=0$. A measurable function $f:X\to[-\infty,\infty]$ has measurable inverse images of Borel sets, where $[-\infty,\infty]$ has its order topology: finite open intervals and the endpoint neighborhoods $[-\infty,a)$ and $(a,\infty]$ form a basis. Its Borel sigma-algebra is generated by these open sets. A complex-valued function is measurable exactly when its finite real and imaginary parts are measurable, equivalently for the usual Borel structure of $\mathbb C$. Almost-everywhere assertions mean outside a measurable $\mu$-null set; completeness of $\mu$ is not assumed. Nonnegative extended addition uses $a+\infty=\infty+a=\infty$ for $a\in[0,\infty]$; positive scalars multiply $\infty$ to $\infty$, while $0\cdot\infty=0$. Signed expressions $\infty-\infty$ remain undefined and are not used in signed integrals. A nonnegative simple function has the form $s=\sum_{j=1}^m c_j\mathbf1_{A_j}$ with finitely many disjoint $A_j\in\Sigma$ and finite $c_j\ge0$. Define $c\mu(A)=+\infty$ if $c>0$ and $\mu(A)=+\infty$, define $0\cdot\infty:=0$, and define the finite sum of these extended nonnegative terms to be $+\infty$ if any term is $+\infty$ and otherwise the real finite sum of [[def-finite-sum]]. Then $\int s\,d\mu:=\sum_j c_j\mu(A_j)$; using canonical level sets $\{s=c\}$ makes this value representation-independent. For measurable $f\ge0$, define $\int f\,d\mu:=\sup\{\int s\,d\mu: s\text{ is simple and }0\le s\le f\}$, using [[def-complete-ordered-field]] for a bounded set of finite values and setting the supremum to $+\infty$ when the values are unbounded or one is infinite. A real measurable $f$ is integrable when $\int|f|\,d\mu<\infty$, and then $\int f:=\int f^+-\int f^-$, where $f^+=\max(f,0)$ and $f^-:=\max(-f,0)$. Complex integrability and integration are defined by integrable real and imaginary parts.

Assign a positive temperature $T$ in kelvins and the exact framework constant $k_{\mathrm B}$ in $\mathrm{J\,K^{-1}}$ from [[def-td-si-quantities]], and put $\beta=(k_{\mathrm B}T)^{-1}$ in $\mathrm{J^{-1}}$. For a finite microstate model $(\Omega,\epsilon)$, adopt the canonical preparation
$$P_\beta(x)=\frac{e^{-\beta E(x)}}{Z(\beta)},\qquad Z(\beta)=\sum_{x\in\Omega}e^{-\beta E(x)}.$$
Here $Z$ is dimensionless, positive, and finite because $\Omega$ is finite and nonempty.

Its nonnegative sums are suprema of finite subsums. The weights $g_i$ are declared model data, not inferred degeneracies or measurements.

Measurability of $E$ means measurability of its numerical coordinate $E/E_*$. The integral convention is [[def-tdmath-measure-integral]] at its current draft definition.

This is an adopted statistical-mechanical preparation rule. It is not derived from the macroscopic thermodynamic laws, a finite bath, entropy maximization, or a time-evolution equation. It does not assert that a physical sample has this preparation; that identification is an additional model assumption to be tested against a specified preparation and apparatus.

Let $(X,\Sigma,\mu)$ be a measure space, let $E:X\to\mathbb R$ be measurable, and let $J\subset\mathbb R$ be open. Suppose $Z(\beta):=\int e^{-\beta E}\,d\mu$ satisfies $0<Z(\beta)<\infty$ on $J$, and for every compact interval $K\subset J$ there is $G_K\in L^1(\mu)$ with $(1+|E|^2)e^{-\beta E}\le G_K$ pointwise for every $\beta\in K$. Define $p_\beta=e^{-\beta E}/Z(\beta)$, $\langle Y\rangle_\beta:=\int Yp_\beta\,d\mu$ for integrable $Y$, and $\operatorname{Var}_\beta(E):=\int(E-\langle E\rangle_\beta)^2p_\beta\,d\mu$. Then $Z\in C^2(J)$, $Z'=-\int E e^{-\beta E}d\mu$, $Z''=\int E^2e^{-\beta E}d\mu$, and $-\partial_\beta\log Z=\langle E\rangle_\beta$, $\partial_\beta^2\log Z=\operatorname{Var}_\beta(E)$. The reference-relative entropy $-\int p_\beta\log p_\beta\,d\mu$ is finite and equals $\log Z+\beta\langle E\rangle_\beta$.

This framework uses the modern International System of Units (SI). A scalar quantity has a real numerical value with the stated unit; a vector quantity has a value in the stated real coordinate space with the stated component unit. The numerical coordinates used elsewhere on this page are divided by their displayed SI units before they are placed in a Euclidean coordinate space.

The model's energy coordinate $U$ and its process-transfer values $Q$ and $W_{\mathrm{on}}$ are scalar energies measured in joules (J). Volume $V$ is a scalar measured in cubic metres (m³); amount of substance $n_j$ for species $j$ is a scalar measured in moles (mol); and a particle count $N_j$, when separately used in a microscopic model, is dimensionless. Time $t$ is measured in seconds (s), mass $M$ in kilograms (kg), and a translational velocity $\mathbf v_{\mathrm{cm}}$ is a vector in $\mathbb R^3$ with components measured in metres per second (m/s). The physical meanings of $U,Q,W_{\mathrm{on}}$ are fixed by the state and process definitions, not by their units alone.

The relevant exact SI relations are

$$1\,\mathrm J=1\,\mathrm{kg\,m^2\,s^{-2}},\qquad 1\,\mathrm N=1\,\mathrm{kg\,m\,s^{-2}},\qquad 1\,\mathrm{Pa}=1\,\mathrm{J\,m^{-3}}.$$

The kelvin (K) is the SI unit of thermodynamic temperature. The Boltzmann constant has the exact defining value $k_{\mathrm B}=1.380649\times10^{-23}\,\mathrm{J\,K^{-1}}$. The mole is the SI unit of amount of substance; the Avogadro constant has the exact defining value $N_{\mathrm A}=6.02214076\times10^{23}\,\mathrm{mol^{-1}}$. When a model uses particle counts, $n_j=N_j/N_{\mathrm A}$. The molar gas constant is derived as $R=N_{\mathrm A}k_{\mathrm B}=8.31446261815324\,\mathrm{J\,mol^{-1}\,K^{-1}}$. This framework does not set $k_{\mathrm B}=1$. These SI definitions do not themselves introduce a thermodynamic temperature state function or entropy function.

Within the macroscopic framework, $(U,V,n_j)$ are adopted state coordinates. A quantity's status as primitive in this model is separate from whether its SI unit is a base or derived unit.

derivations.claim: Apply [L1] with numerical energy $e=E/E_*$ and $b=E_*\beta$. Any compact interval $K_b\subset J_b$ corresponds to $K_b/E_*\subset J_\beta$, so its domination hypothesis is exactly the stated dimensionless envelope. The equality $be=\beta E$ identifies $\widetilde Z(b)=Z(b/E_*)$ and the normalized density with [F2]. The supplier gives finite first and second moments of $e$; hence $\langle E\rangle_\beta=E_*\langle e\rangle_b$ and $\operatorname{Var}_\beta(E)=E_*^2\operatorname{Var}_b(e)$ are finite. All weighted functions and difference quotients are measurable functions of $e$, so the argument requires no completeness of $\mu$.

Since $Z(\beta)=\widetilde Z(E_*\beta)$, substitution of $\Delta b=E_*\Delta\beta$ in derivative difference quotients multiplies first derivatives by $E_*$ and second derivatives by $E_*^2$. Thus [L1] yields $Z\in C^2$ and the stated log-derivative mean and variance identities in joules and joules squared. The density is unchanged, so its absolutely integrable relative entropy is $s_\beta=\log\widetilde Z+b\langle e\rangle_b=\log Z+\beta\langle E\rangle_\beta$. Multiplying by $k_{\mathrm B}$ gives $S_\beta$ in $\mathrm{J\,K^{-1}}$; using $\beta k_{\mathrm B}=1/T$ gives $F_{\mathrm{stat}}=\langle E\rangle_\beta-TS_\beta=-k_{\mathrm B}T\log Z$. This is conditional on the declared sampling model and the stated hypotheses of the current draft mathematical supplier.

case_scope.source_excerpt: Let $(X,\Sigma,\mu)$ be a measure space with dimensionless reference measure, let $E:X\to\mathbb R\,\mathrm J$ be a finite physical energy, and let $J_\beta\subset(0,\infty)$ be an open inverse-temperature set in $\mathrm{J^{-1}}$. Set $E_*=1\,\mathrm J$, $e=E/E_*:X\to\mathbb R$, $b=E_*\beta$, and $J_b=E_*J_\beta$; measurability of $E$ means measurability of the dimensionless numerical coordinate $e$. Suppose $Z(\beta)=\int_Xe^{-\beta E}\,d\mu$ is positive and finite on $J_\beta$, and for each compact $K\subset J_\beta$ there is an integrable $G_K\ge0$ with $(1+|e|^2)e^{-\beta E}=(1+|e|^2)e^{-be}\le G_K$ for every $\beta\in K$. Under the canonical sampling assumption [[post-td-canonical-sampling]], define $p_\beta=e^{-\beta E}/Z$, $\langle E\rangle_\beta=\int E p_\beta\,d\mu$, and $\operatorname{Var}_\beta(E)=\int(E-\langle E\rangle_\beta)^2p_\beta\,d\mu$. Then $Z\in C^2$, $-\partial_\beta\log Z=\langle E\rangle_\beta$, $\partial_\beta^2\log Z=\operatorname{Var}_\beta(E)$, and the relative Gibbs entropy is finite with $S_\beta=-k_{\mathrm B}\int p_\beta\log p_\beta\,d\mu=k_{\mathrm B}(\log Z+\beta\langle E\rangle_\beta)$. Hence $F_{\mathrm{stat}}=-k_{\mathrm B}T\log Z=\langle E\rangle_\beta-TS_\beta$ for $\beta=(k_{\mathrm B}T)^{-1}$.

Parameter difference quotients and limits are measurable compositions of the measurable finite energy; local integrable second-moment envelope dominates derivatives of orders 1,2 and proves continuity by dominated convergence, even on a noncomplete measure space. Positive finite Z normalizes; finite absolute first moment gives absolute entropy convergence. Entropy is relative to dimensionless reference measure and need not be nonnegative. No arbitrary phase measure or empirical identification is inferred. Native u15 repair review: the real supplier is applied to e=E/(1 J), b=(1 J)beta with the same reference measure or g_i=1. Finite moments and absolute entropy convergence follow from the full inspected supplier proof. Original physical identities are preserved; no independent review or publication acceptance is claimed.

citations.quote:
**(a) Adopted readings and restricted sector class.** Adopt the observable and
probability postulate [[post-nrqm-framework-observable-and-probability]] (P2)
and the autonomous-dynamics postulate
[[post-nrqm-framework-autonomous-dynamics]] (P4), in the readings of
[[def-nrqm-observables-framework-observable-and-outcome-law]] and
[[def-nrqm-autonomous-dynamics-framework-evolution]], for the declared
fixed-$N$ model of
[[def-nrqm-many-body-framework-declared-fixed-n-model]]. This definition
applies to the class of declared models whose sector space
$\mathfrak H_N^\sigma$ is **finite-dimensional**, in particular to every
finite-mode realization
([[def-nrqm-identical-particles-framework-orbital-occupation-model]]), where
$D:=\dim\mathfrak H_N^\sigma$ is finite (and may be zero) by
[[thm-nrqm-identical-particles-finite-mode-occupation-counts]] clauses (a),
(b). Write $\mathcal D(\mathfrak H_N^\sigma)$ for the set of declared sector
preparations, that is, the density operators on $\mathfrak H_N^\sigma$
([[lem-nrqm-composites-density-and-scalar-spectral-probability]] clause (a)).
If $D=0$, the only operator has trace zero, so
$\mathcal D(\mathfrak H_N^\sigma)=\varnothing$. The partition trace is
$Z_N=0$, and there is no normalized canonical density or equilibrium free
energy; $\log D$, $D^{-1}\mathrm{id}$ and $\log Z_N$ are not used in this
branch. Clauses (b), (d) and (e) below apply when $D\ge1$; the assigned
parameters of (c) can still be declared when $D=0$.
Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice ([[def-countable-choice]]).

**(b) Dimensionless entropy.** For $\rho\in\mathcal D(\mathfrak H_N^\sigma)$
with eigenvalues $w_1,\dots,w_D\ge0$ (counted with multiplicity, in any
order), the **entropy** of $\rho$ is
$$s(\rho):=-\sum_{i:\,w_i>0}w_i\log w_i\in[0,\log D],$$
the quantity of [[thm-nrqm-fock-and-equilibrium-finite-gibbs-free-energy-minimum]]
clause (a) with $\log$ the natural logarithm
([[def-natural-logarithm]]). It is dimensionless, is a function of the
eigenvalue multiset of $\rho$ alone, and equals zero exactly for pure
preparations; by clause (c) of the cited theorem $s(\rho)=\log D$ holds
exactly when $\rho=D^{-1}\mathrm{id}$.

**(c) Boltzmann constant, temperature and inverse temperature.** The model
assigns a positive **Boltzmann constant** $k_B$ and a positive **temperature**
$T$; in the SI conventions of
[[def-nrqm-framework-quantities-and-units]] the unit of $k_B$ is
$\mathrm J\,\mathrm K^{-1}$, the unit of $T$ is the kelvin, and
$$k_B=1.380\,649\times10^{-23}\ \mathrm J\,\mathrm K^{-1}$$
fixed exactly by the BIPM SI definition. The model declares the **inverse
temperature** $\beta:=1/(k_BT)$, a positive real number in $\mathrm J^{-1}$.
The value and exactness of $k_B$ are unit-convention facts; the assignment of
the parameter $T$ to a physical sample, and the identification of
$\beta=1/(k_BT)$ with an inverse thermodynamic temperature, are adopted
assumptions of the ensemble model of this pair, not consequences of P1-P4,
and are tested identifications with uncertainty under the preparation and
apparatus postulate [[post-nrqm-framework-preparation-and-apparatus]] (P7),
whose clauses (i), (iii) and (iv) require a declared comparison and
calibration model and qualifications for measured inputs. No thermometer,
calibration or measured temperature is supplied here.

**(d) Physical entropy.** The **physical entropy** of $\rho$ is
$$S(\rho):=k_B\,s(\rho),$$
read in $\mathrm J\,\mathrm K^{-1}$. It is nonnegative, is at most
$k_B\log D$, and vanishes exactly for pure preparations.

**(e) Free-energy functional.** For $\rho\in\mathcal D(\mathfrak H_N^\sigma)$,
let $\operatorname{tr}(\rho H_N^\sigma)\in\mathbb R$ be the mean of the
declared energy observable in $\rho$ (finite because $D<\infty$, in the
moment reading of
[[def-nrqm-observables-framework-observable-and-outcome-law]] clause (e)).
The **Helmholtz free-energy reading** of $\rho$ is
$$F(\rho):=\operatorname{tr}(\rho H_N^\sigma)-k_BT\,s(\rho),$$
read in joules; it is the quantity
$\operatorname{tr}(\rho H)-\beta^{-1}s(\rho)$ of
[[thm-nrqm-fock-and-equilibrium-finite-gibbs-free-energy-minimum]] clause (a)
at the identified $\beta$. For the canonical operator
$\rho_\beta:=e^{-\beta H_N^\sigma}/Z_N$ and
$Z_N:=\operatorname{tr}e^{-\beta H_N^\sigma}\in(0,\infty)$ (positive finite sum in the
nonzero finite-dimensional sector), the number $F_{\mathrm{eq}}:=-\beta^{-1}\log Z_N$
is called the **equilibrium free energy**; it is the value of the functional
at $\rho_\beta$ by the cited theorem.

**(f) Scope.** This definition covers only declared models with
finite-dimensional sector space, with the zero-sector branch of (a), and preparations in
$\mathcal D(\mathfrak H_N^\sigma)$. For a declared spatial realization, whose
sector space is infinite-dimensional, the operator $\rho\log\rho$ need not be
trace class; no entropy, physical entropy or free energy is defined here for
that case, and a separate trace-class statement would be required. The
definition asserts no increase of entropy in time, no equilibration to
$\rho_\beta$, no thermodynamic limit, no pressure or volume variable, and no
measured temperature, entropy or free energy.

**(a) Adopted readings and framework data.** Adopt the state and composition
postulate [[post-nrqm-framework-state-and-composition]] (P1), the observable
and probability postulate
[[post-nrqm-framework-observable-and-probability]] (P2), the
autonomous-dynamics postulate [[post-nrqm-framework-autonomous-dynamics]]
(P4) and the preparation and apparatus postulate
[[post-nrqm-framework-preparation-and-apparatus]] (P7), together with the
Boltzmann-constant and temperature conventions of
[[def-nrqm-many-body-framework-entropy-and-free-energy]]. Declare one of the
following model readings of the same **adopted Gibbs assignment**:

(i) a fixed-$N$ model of
[[def-nrqm-many-body-framework-declared-fixed-n-model]], on its sector space,
with Gibbs generator $G:=H_N^\sigma$; or

(ii) a separately declared number-variable mode model, such as a one-mode
bosonic Fock space, a fermionic occupation space, or a declared countable
independent-mode space, with its declared assigned observables and energy
operator $H$. The model declares a self-adjoint Gibbs generator $G$ on that
space: either $G=H$, or a separately supplied self-adjoint realization of the
effective generator $G=H-\mu\mathcal N$, where $\mathcal N$ is the declared
particle-number operator and $\mu\in\mathbb R$ is an assigned chemical
potential in joules. The subtraction is an operator with its supplied domain,
not an assertion that a formal unbounded difference is self-adjoint.

In either reading assume $G$ is bounded below and give its spectral PVM
$E_G$ ([[thm-spectral-theorem-for-unbounded-self-adjoint-operators]],
[[def-projection-valued-measure]]). Let $T>0$ be an assigned temperature in
kelvin and let $\beta:=1/(k_BT)$ in $\mathrm J^{-1}$ with the assigned
Boltzmann constant $k_B$. The Gibbs assignment to either model, and the
chemical-potential identification in (ii), are additional physical
preparation assumptions made here; they are not derived from P1-P4 or from
the fixed-$N$ construction. In (ii) no restriction on the assigned real
$\mu$ is imposed beyond the declared generator and trace existence
conditions; the mode-specific convergence conditions are proved separately.
For reading (ii), $G$ specifies the Gibbs weights. If the assigned autonomous
dynamics is generated by $H$, stationarity of the Gibbs density requires its
separate dynamical or commutation hypotheses; this assignment does not
identify $H-\mu\mathcal N$ with the physical evolution generator.
The physical Helmholtz free-energy vocabulary of the entropy definition
continues to apply only to its stated nonzero finite-sector class and is not
extended to every effective generator by this postulate.
Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice and the Axiom of Choice
([[def-countable-choice]], [[def-axiom-of-choice]]), the choice hypotheses of
the spectral calculus.

**(b) Existence hypothesis and the Gibbs preparation.** The model assumes
that the **partition trace is strictly positive and finite**:
$$0<Z:=\operatorname{Tr}e^{-\beta G}<\infty,$$
where $\operatorname{Tr}B:=\sum_{f\in\mathcal B}\langle Bf,f\rangle$ for a
bounded positive $B$ and an orthonormal basis $\mathcal B$, with value allowed
to be $+\infty$. Such a basis exists under the declared AC by the maximal
orthonormal-family argument using [[thm-zorn]] and the zero-complement
criterion of [[thm-parseval-equivalences-for-a-complete-orthonormal-family]].
This trace is basis independent: for $C:=B^{1/2}$ of
[[thm-positive-square-root]], the defining sum is
$\sum_{f\in\mathcal B}\|Cf\|^2$, whose invariance is
[[thm-hilbert-schmidt-norm-is-basis-independent]]. When the sum is finite,
$C$ is Hilbert-Schmidt ([[def-hilbert-schmidt-operator]]), so $B=C^2$ is
trace class by [[thm-trace-class-iff-product-of-two-hilbert-schmidt-operators]],
and its ordinary trace is this same diagonal sum by
[[thm-trace-is-absolutely-convergent-and-basis-independent]]. Apply this to the bounded positive operator $e^{-\beta G}$, since the
declared Gibbs generator $G$ is bounded below. The model
adopts as the **canonical** or **Gibbs preparation** of the declared model
at temperature $T$ the density operator
$$\rho_\beta:=Z^{-1}e^{-\beta G}.$$
If the sector is zero-dimensional, its partition trace is $Z=0$, no
trace-one density exists, and no canonical density or equilibrium free
energy is assigned. On a nonzero finite-dimensional model space, $Z$ is a
positive finite sum $\sum_je^{-\beta E_j}$ over the eigenvalues of $G$; no energy
sign restriction is needed. There $\rho_\beta$ is the canonical operator of
[[thm-nrqm-fock-and-equilibrium-finite-gibbs-free-energy-minimum]], and the
strict positivity and finiteness hypothesis is automatic. In reading (i),
$Z=Z_N$ and this is precisely the finite-sector Gibbs assignment.

Outside the finite-dimensional class the existence hypothesis is a genuine
restriction. For a declared non-interacting fixed-$N$ model with a supplied
countably infinite orthonormal eigenmode basis and real mode energies
$\varepsilon_j$ bounded below, the complete construction and trace criterion
of [[lem-nrqm-many-body-fixed-n-countable-mode-partition-criterion]] give
$Z_N=h_N(q)$ for bosonic statistics or $Z_N=e_N(q)$ for fermionic statistics,
where $q_j=e^{-\beta\varepsilon_j}$ and $h_N,e_N$ are the corresponding
nonnegative occupation-series sums. For every fixed $N\ge1$, either trace is
finite exactly when $\sum_jq_j<\infty$. This is a trace on the fixed-$N$
sector and permits negative mode energies.

For the separately declared full bosonic Fock models of reading (ii),
the single-mode calculation of
[[thm-nrqm-fock-and-equilibrium-single-mode-thermal-trace]] and the product
criterion of [[thm-nrqm-fock-and-equilibrium-countable-mode-product-criterion]]
provide the separate mathematical full-Fock traces, with their original
positive mode-energy hypotheses: they sum over every particle number,
including the vacuum, giving $(1-e^{-\beta\varepsilon})^{-1}$ for one mode
and $\prod_j(1-e^{-\beta\varepsilon_j})^{-1}$ for countably many modes.
Their physical Gibbs reading is the additional assignment of (a)(ii), not a
consequence of a mathematical trace formula. Those full-Fock traces are not
substituted for the fixed-$N$ partition trace of reading (i).

**(c) The equilibrium assumption and thermal means.** The model **assumes**
that, for a declared sample of the species at the assigned temperature $T$
and in the absence of further preparation information, the preparation
description of the sample is $\rho_\beta$ in the sense of P1. For an assigned
sharp observable $(A,u_A)$ with spectral PVM $E_A$, define its outcome law
$\mu_{\rho_\beta}^A(B):=\operatorname{tr}(\rho_\beta E_A(B))$ as in
[[def-nrqm-observables-framework-observable-and-outcome-law]] clause (b).
If and only if the absolute first moment is finite,
$$\int_{\mathbb R}|a|\,d\mu_{\rho_\beta}^A(a)<\infty,$$
the model defines the **thermal mean** at temperature $T$ by
$$\langle A\rangle_\beta:=\int_{\mathbb R}a\,d\mu_{\rho_\beta}^A(a),$$
read in the assigned unit $u_A$. For bounded $A$ this equals
$\operatorname{tr}(\rho_\beta A)=\operatorname{tr}(A\rho_\beta)$. For
unbounded $A$, if the mean exists and the literal product $A\rho_\beta$ is
defined on the whole Hilbert space and is trace class, the mean also equals
$\operatorname{tr}(A\rho_\beta)$ and
$\operatorname{tr}(\overline{\rho_\beta A})$; these conditional product
identities are proved by the density eigenexpansion in
[[lem-nrqm-many-body-spectral-mean-and-defined-trace-product]]. First-moment
existence alone imposes no such product or operator-square-domain condition.
When the absolute first moment is infinite the model asserts no finite
thermal mean. The identification of the parameter $T$ with the thermodynamic temperature of a
sample, and of $\beta$ with its inverse temperature, is part of this
assumption; the stated conservation and equilibrium properties of
$\rho_\beta$ under the flow of P4, and the extremal property of $\rho_\beta$
among preparations, are separate conditional results of this pair.

**(d) Motivation and status.** The assumption is motivated, but not
established, by the maximum-entropy reasoning of the cited sources: among
preparations with a prescribed mean energy, the Gibbs weights maximize the
entropy functional, and the finite-dimensional comparison theorem makes
$\rho_\beta$ the minimizer of the corresponding functional built from $G$.
Its physical Helmholtz free-energy reading applies in the stated finite
fixed-sector class; an effective-generator interpretation in a different
mode model is a separate declared reading. That reasoning is
an argument inside mathematical statistics and thermodynamics; it does not
derive the physical assumption that a sample is described by $\rho_\beta$.
The postulate is an **adopted** statistical-mechanical assumption of the
model, in the sense of the content model's distinction between adopted
assumptions and derived consequences.

**(e) Scope.** The postulate asserts nothing about how a sample reaches the
Gibbs preparation; in particular it asserts no thermalization, no equilibration
time, no ergodicity, no master-equation or Markov approximation, no
thermodynamic limit, no pressure, volume or phase-transition structure, and
no measured temperature or expectation. The requirement $0<Z<\infty$ is part
of the assumption; the model does not define a canonical preparation when
$Z=0$ or the partition trace diverges. Any comparison with a laboratory sample requires the
declared preparation, isolation, detection and sampling models of P7, and
agreement of a thermal prediction with data is evidence about the combined
model and apparatus assumptions, not a proof of the framework or of this
postulate.

Adopt the canonical equilibrium-ensemble postulate
[[post-nrqm-many-body-canonical-equilibrium-ensemble]] together with the
state, probability, dynamics and preparation postulates P1, P2, P4, P7
([[post-nrqm-framework-state-and-composition]],
[[post-nrqm-framework-observable-and-probability]],
[[post-nrqm-framework-autonomous-dynamics]],
[[post-nrqm-framework-preparation-and-apparatus]]) in the readings of
[[def-nrqm-many-body-framework-entropy-and-free-energy]] and
[[def-nrqm-observables-framework-observable-and-outcome-law]], and assume the
Axiom of Countable Choice ([[def-countable-choice]]). Work in the
finite-dimensional sector class of the entropy definition: the declared
fixed-$N$ model of
[[def-nrqm-many-body-framework-declared-fixed-n-model]] has sector space
$\mathfrak H_N^\sigma$ of finite dimension $D\ge1$ with self-adjoint energy
operator $H_N^\sigma$, assigned temperature $T>0$, inverse temperature
$\beta=1/(k_BT)$ and eigen-decomposition
$H_N^\sigma=\sum_{j=1}^DE_jT_{v_j,v_j}$ with orthonormal eigenbasis
$(v_1,\dots,v_D)$ and real eigenvalues $E_1,\dots,E_D$. Write
$q_j:=e^{-\beta E_j}/Z_N$ with $Z_N:=\sum_je^{-\beta E_j}$,
$\rho_\beta:=\sum_jq_jT_{v_j,v_j}$, and let
$F(\rho)=\operatorname{tr}(\rho H_N^\sigma)-k_BT\,s(\rho)$ and
$F_{\mathrm{eq}}:=-k_BT\log Z_N$ be the free-energy functional and
equilibrium free energy of
[[def-nrqm-many-body-framework-entropy-and-free-energy]] clauses (e).
Then:

(a) *the canonical preparation*: $Z_N\in(0,\infty)$ is a finite sum,
$q_j>0$, $\sum_jq_j=1$, and $\rho_\beta$ is a declared sector preparation of
the model with
$$\operatorname{tr}(\rho_\beta H_N^\sigma)=\frac1{Z_N}\sum_{j=1}^DE_je^{-\beta E_j},\qquad s(\rho_\beta)=\log Z_N+\beta\operatorname{tr}(\rho_\beta H_N^\sigma);$$

(b) *free-energy minimum*: for every declared sector preparation $\rho$ one
has $F(\rho)\ge F_{\mathrm{eq}}=-k_BT\log Z_N$;

(c) *uniqueness*: equality $F(\rho)=F_{\mathrm{eq}}$ holds if and only if
$\rho=\rho_\beta$; consequently the canonical preparation is the unique
minimiser of the free-energy functional over the declared sector
preparations, and $F(\rho_\beta)=F_{\mathrm{eq}}$;

(d) *degenerate case*: if $H_N^\sigma=c\,\mathrm{id}$ for a real $c$, then
$Z_N=De^{-\beta c}$, $\rho_\beta=D^{-1}\mathrm{id}$,
$s(\rho_\beta)=\log D$ and $F_{\mathrm{eq}}=c-k_BT\log D$;

(e) *scope*: the statement is conditional on the adopted ensemble postulate
and on the declared finite-dimensional model; it asserts no equilibration of
any preparation towards $\rho_\beta$, no rate of approach, no thermodynamic
limit, no pressure or volume variable, and, for a laboratory sample, it
inherits the tested identification of the preparation and temperature
assignment of P7.

**(a) Dimensions.** Write $\ell$, $\tau$, $\mu$, $\vartheta$ for the four independent dimension symbols of length, duration, mass and electric charge. A **dimension** is an element of $\mathbb Q^{4}$, written $\ell^{a}\tau^{b}\mu^{c}\vartheta^{d}$ with $a,b,c,d\in\mathbb Q$; products and inverses of dimensions are componentwise addition and negation, and the dimensionless dimension $\ell^{0}\tau^{0}\mu^{0}\vartheta^{0}$ is abbreviated $1$. The conventions assign to each quantity of the framework a dimension $[X]$, subject to $[XY]=[X][Y]$, $[X/Y]=[X][Y]^{-1}$ and $[dX/du]=[X][u]^{-1}$, with sums meaningful only between quantities of equal dimension, in which case the sum carries that dimension. For a rational power $q$, dimension powers mean $[X]^q=\ell^{qa}\tau^{qb}\mu^{qc}\vartheta^{qd}$ when $[X]=\ell^{a}\tau^{b}\mu^{c}\vartheta^{d}$. Rational exponents include the half-integer wave-function dimensions in clause (d); the integer-exponent dimensions form the subgroup $\mathbb Z^4$. These are consistency requirements on the conventions, not laws of nature.

For extensions using temperature, adjoin an independent dimension symbol $\Theta$: the enlarged group is $\mathbb Q^4\times\mathbb Q$, written $\ell^a\tau^b\mu^c\vartheta^d\Theta^e$, with the same componentwise rules. The preceding group embeds by $e=0$, so all previously assigned dimensions are preserved. Temperature has dimension $\Theta$, the Boltzmann constant has dimension $\mu\ell^2\tau^{-2}\Theta^{-1}$, and entropy in joules per kelvin has that same dimension; a dimensionless entropy remains dimensionless. This convention does not assign a temperature or an entropy to any system.

**(b) Reference units.** The **metre** (m), **second** (s), **kilogram** (kg) and **coulomb** (C) are the reference units of length, duration, mass and charge; a quantity of dimension $\ell^{a}\tau^{b}\mu^{c}\vartheta^{d}$ is expressed in the unit $\mathrm m^{a}\mathrm s^{b}\mathrm kg^{c}\mathrm C^{d}$. Coordinates of an inertial frame are read with the time coordinate $t$ in seconds, $[t]=\tau$, and the spatial coordinates $x_{i}$ in metres, $[x_{i}]=\ell$; slice distances of the arena are read in metres. In the temperature extension the reference unit of $\Theta$ is the kelvin (K), so the general reference unit gains a factor $\mathrm K^e$.

**(c) Defining constants of the current SI.** The framework keeps $\hbar$ explicit. In the current SI the constants $h$, $c$ and $e$ are exact defining constants, with the values $h=6{,}626\,070\,15\times10^{-34}$ J s, $c=2{,}99792458\times10^{8}$ m s$^{-1}$ and $e=1{,}602\,176\,634\times10^{-19}$ C, and $\hbar:=h/(2\pi)$. These are real scalar constants with dimensions and units $[h]=[\hbar]=\mu\ell^{2}\tau^{-1}$ (J s), $[c]=\ell\tau^{-1}$ (m s$^{-1}$), and $[e]=\vartheta$ (C). The vacuum permeability $\mu_{0}$ is a positive real scalar that is experimentally determined in the current SI, with $[\mu_{0}]=\mu\ell\vartheta^{-2}$ (N A$^{-2}$ = H m$^{-1}$); $\varepsilon_{0}:=(\mu_{0}c^{2})^{-1}$ is a positive real scalar with $[\varepsilon_{0}]=\mu^{-1}\ell^{-3}\tau^{2}\vartheta^{2}$ (F m$^{-1}$). These are unit-convention statements of the SI, not measurements reported by this framework; $c$ enters the framework only through the separate radiation assumptions adopted on their own pages, not in the nonrelativistic spacetime of [[def-nrqm-framework-newtonian-spacetime]].

**(d) Dimensions and types of the framework's quantities.** The dimension map is fixed on the following quantities.

1. State quantities: a position wave function of a system with $d$ spatial dimensions and $r$ internal components is an almost-everywhere equivalence class in $L^{2}(\mathbb R^{d};\mathbb C^{r})$ with dimension $\ell^{-d/2}$, its norm $\|\psi\|$ is dimensionless, and an abstract normalized state and the density operators of the state postulate are dimensionless.
2. Probability: the outcome probability $\mu(B)$ of the observable postulate is a dimensionless number; a position density $|\psi|^{2}$ has dimension $\ell^{-d}$; a momentum wave function normalized against $\mathrm d^{d}p$ has dimension $(\mu\ell\tau^{-1})^{-d/2}$; an amplitude for a finite outcome is a dimensionless complex number, while an amplitude read against a detector coordinate carries the square-root of the inverse of the detector measure.
3. Frame parameters ([[def-nrqm-framework-galilei-transformations]]): $[b]=\tau$, $[a_{i}]=\ell$, $[v_{i}]=\ell\tau^{-1}$ and $[R_{ij}]=1$.
4. Mechanical quantities: action $[\hbar]=\mu\ell^{2}\tau^{-1}$; energy and the Hamiltonian eigenvalues $\mu\ell^{2}\tau^{-2}$; momentum $\mu\ell\tau^{-1}$; position components $\ell$; angular momentum and spin $\mu\ell^{2}\tau^{-1}$; mass $\mu$; velocity of a free spinless model $\ell\tau^{-1}$; force $\mu\ell\tau^{-2}$; a real potential energy $\mu\ell^{2}\tau^{-2}$.
5. Probability current: in the ordinary continuous-field regime, fix an integer $d\ge1$, an open spatial region $\Omega\subseteq\mathbb R^d$ and an open time interval $I\subseteq\mathbb R$. A **probability current density** is a declared continuous map $j:\Omega\times I\to\mathbb R^d$, whose spatial components have dimension $\ell^{1-d}\tau^{-1}$ and reference unit $\mathrm m^{1-d}\mathrm s^{-1}$. At fixed time it is a spatial vector field; its signed normal component is read as probability transported per unit spatial $(d-1)$-area and time. Explicitly, for a flat face $S=\{x:x_k=a,\ a_i\le x_i\le b_i\ (i\ne k)\}\subset\Omega$, with $a_i<b_i$ and chosen normal $n=\epsilon e_k$, $\epsilon\in\{-1,1\}$, define its **signed probability flux** at $t\in I$ as $\Phi_S(t):=\epsilon\int_{\prod_{i\ne k}[a_i,b_i]}j_k(x_1,\ldots,x_{k-1},a,x_{k+1},\ldots,x_d,t)\prod_{i\ne k}dx_i$. Here $e_k$ is the $k$th coordinate unit vector and the integral uses $(d-1)$-dimensional Lebesgue measure; for $d=1$ this means $\Phi_{\{a\}}(t)=\epsilon j(a,t)$. The flux has dimension $\tau^{-1}$ and unit $\mathrm s^{-1}$; positive sign means transport in the chosen normal direction. Fluxes through curved surfaces, or currents with weaker regularity, require separately specified surface measures or traces. This fixes the quantity type and flux convention; it supplies neither a current associated to an arbitrary $L^2$ state nor a conservation or detector law. Each dynamical model supplies its current construction and balance hypotheses.
6. Electric quantities of the model parameters: charge has dimension $\vartheta$; a magnetic moment has dimension $\ell^{2}\vartheta\tau^{-1}$, equivalently $\mathrm A\,\mathrm m^{2}=\mathrm J\,\mathrm T^{-1}$, and a gyromagnetic parameter $\gamma$ in the relation $\boldsymbol\mu=\gamma\mathbf S$ has dimension $\mu^{-1}\vartheta$, equivalently $\mathrm s^{-1}\mathrm T^{-1}$; these quantities appear only in the model assumptions that introduce them.
7. Statistical quantities: a mean has the dimension of its outcome coordinate, a variance the square of it and a standard deviation it; a mean, variance or higher moment exists only when the corresponding moment of the outcome probability is finite, so a symbolic average is not a number unless that integrability is established. Angles and phases are dimensionless under the radian convention.
8. Quantities of later extension assumptions - radiation frequencies and energies, electric dipole moments, cross sections, temperatures and entropies - are declared with their dimensions and units by the items that introduce those assumptions, under the rules fixed here; they are not part of the present list.

**(e) Conventions only.** No numerical value of any model parameter is fixed by this item: no mass, charge, spin label, potential or measured constant is asserted, and natural-unit shorthand (for example setting $\hbar=1$ or $c=1$) is read as an abbreviation for the corresponding SI-dimensioned statement with the constant restored.

This framework uses the modern International System of Units (SI). A scalar quantity has a real numerical value with the stated unit; a vector quantity has a value in the stated real coordinate space with the stated component unit. The numerical coordinates used elsewhere on this page are divided by their displayed SI units before they are placed in a Euclidean coordinate space.

The model's energy coordinate $U$ and its process-transfer values $Q$ and $W_{\mathrm{on}}$ are scalar energies measured in joules (J). Volume $V$ is a scalar measured in cubic metres (m³); amount of substance $n_j$ for species $j$ is a scalar measured in moles (mol); and a particle count $N_j$, when separately used in a microscopic model, is dimensionless. Time $t$ is measured in seconds (s), mass $M$ in kilograms (kg), and a translational velocity $\mathbf v_{\mathrm{cm}}$ is a vector in $\mathbb R^3$ with components measured in metres per second (m/s). The physical meanings of $U,Q,W_{\mathrm{on}}$ are fixed by the state and process definitions, not by their units alone.

The relevant exact SI relations are

$$1\,\mathrm J=1\,\mathrm{kg\,m^2\,s^{-2}},\qquad 1\,\mathrm N=1\,\mathrm{kg\,m\,s^{-2}},\qquad 1\,\mathrm{Pa}=1\,\mathrm{J\,m^{-3}}.$$

The kelvin (K) is the SI unit of thermodynamic temperature. The Boltzmann constant has the exact defining value $k_{\mathrm B}=1.380649\times10^{-23}\,\mathrm{J\,K^{-1}}$. The mole is the SI unit of amount of substance; the Avogadro constant has the exact defining value $N_{\mathrm A}=6.02214076\times10^{23}\,\mathrm{mol^{-1}}$. When a model uses particle counts, $n_j=N_j/N_{\mathrm A}$. The molar gas constant is derived as $R=N_{\mathrm A}k_{\mathrm B}=8.31446261815324\,\mathrm{J\,mol^{-1}\,K^{-1}}$. This framework does not set $k_{\mathrm B}=1$. These SI definitions do not themselves introduce a thermodynamic temperature state function or entropy function.

Within the macroscopic framework, $(U,V,n_j)$ are adopted state coordinates. A quantity's status as primitive in this model is separate from whether its SI unit is a base or derived unit.

derivations.claim: The finite-sector class, assigned positive temperature, canonical preparation, and entropy functional in the Statement are exactly the hypotheses and definitions of [F1]–[F2]. Countable Choice is stated explicitly in [A1], as required by [F2].

By [F2], every declared sector preparation obeys $F(\rho)\ge-k_{\mathrm B}T\log Z_N$, with equality only for the canonical preparation. Replacing $\beta^{-1}$ by $k_{\mathrm B}T$ using [F1]–[F3] gives the displayed minimum and units. This is a conditional preparation-model deduction, not a claim that dynamics reaches the minimizer.

case_scope.source_excerpt:
Work in the nonzero finite-dimensional fixed-$N$ sector of [[def-nrqm-many-body-framework-entropy-and-free-energy]], with self-adjoint energy $H_N^\sigma$ in joules and assigned $T>0$ in kelvins. Adopt the Gibbs preparation of [[post-nrqm-many-body-canonical-equilibrium-ensemble]] and its unit convention $\beta=(k_{\mathrm B}T)^{-1}$. For $F(\rho)=\operatorname{tr}(\rho H_N^\sigma)-T S(\rho)$ over the declared sector density operators, the canonical preparation is the unique minimizer and
$$\min_\rho F(\rho)=F_{\mathrm{eq}}=-k_{\mathrm B}T\log\operatorname{tr}(e^{-\beta H_N^\sigma}).$$
This quantum statistical functional is not identified here with a macroscopic Helmholtz potential without an additional model bridge; its minimum does not establish equilibration.
